transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Miguel (Redwood AE), Emily (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood Product), Liam (ByteWave Head of ML), Priya (ByteWave ML Eng), Marcus (ByteWave Infra)

Summary (auto):
Short walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles with INT8 and FP8. Focus on quality vs latency tradeoffs, expected token-level latency wins, throughput on Dedicated pools, and security/VPC questions. Agreed to run pilot with ByteWave workload and share benchmark sheet.

Topics:
- Quantization modes: INT8 vs FP8
- Quality regression measurement and evals
- Latency and throughput tradeoffs on Dedicated GPUs
- KV/prefix cache impact and batching
- Security: KMS, VPC, SOC2

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Miguel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Miguel from Redwood, AE on the account, with Emily our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:05] Liam: Good, thanks. Do a quick intro from our side, Liam here, Priya and Marcus on.
[00:00:15] Emily: Awesome. We'll jump into an Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles, INT8 and FP8, and show some quality vs latency charts. Quick note — audio might have a couple of stutters, we've got a recording.
[00:00:30] Priya: Sounds good. We're mostly evaluating how much latency we'd save with INT8 vs FP8 and what's the quality hit, if any. Our SLO is 150ms p95 for short responses (~40-60 tokens).
[00:00:45] Miguel: Perfect. We'll show typical numbers and then propose a pilot on your sample workload. Emily, take it away.
[00:00:50] Emily: Sure. Slide 1 — quick recap of Redwood Optimize. We recommend quant profiles by workload: INT8 for max latency/throughput wins, FP8 as a middle ground with smaller quality regression. Note, sometimes transcription shows FP8 as F-P eight or something, so ignore that.
[00:01:10] Emily: Here's an example chart; on A100-class Dedicated, INT8 gave ~35-45% lower token latency vs FP32 baseline, and FP8 gave ~20-30%. Throughput improved accordingly. These are illustrative — actual numbers depend on sequence length, KV cache hit rate, and batching policies.
[00:01:30] Liam: Wait, 35-45% on INT8 — what's the quality delta? We can't tolerate hallucination increases.
[00:01:40] Emily: Great question. We run evals on your prompt set. For many models we see <1.5% drop in accuracy on our typical open-domain evals for INT8 with tuned quant params, and <0.7% for FP8. But that varies. INT8 can introduce edge-case regressions for tasks requiring fine numeric precision or long-range context.
[00:02:05] Priya: By accuracy do you mean token-level perplexity or downstream metric?
[00:02:10] Emily: Both — we measure perplexity, exact-match for retrieval/rerank tasks, and end-to-end downstream QA F1 where applicable. We provide the eval harness so you can run your own holdout set.
[00:02:25] Marcus: For our infra, the big concern is latency variance under burst. How does batching interact with quantization?
[00:02:35] Emily: Quantization primarily reduces compute per token; batching still gives throughput benefits but can add latency. On Dedicated you can set autoscale and burst pools. For low p95 we recommend smaller batch sizes with INT8 and aggressive prefix/KV caching to avoid recompute.
[00:02:50] Miguel: Also, routing policies can send low-latency critical requests to higher tiers or to an FP8 profile if you need the quality; Redwood can failover automatically.
[00:03:05] Liam: Cool. Can you run a quick demo of a side-by-side? Maybe a short prompt through FP32, FP8, INT8?
[00:03:12] Emily: Yep, I have a pre-run comparison. I'll paste three outputs and show the latency numbers. Note the transcript may lowercase some names — the demo output is verbatim.
[00:03:30] [00:03:30] Emily: FP32 (baseline) — 48ms avg token latency; reply: "The weather in London is ..."
[00:03:45] [00:03:45] Emily: FP8 — 34ms avg token latency; reply: "The weather in London is ..." (practically identical for this prompt)
[00:03:58] [00:03:58] Emily: INT8 — 27ms avg token latency; reply: "The weather in London is ..." (small grammatic variance: "the weather in london looks..." — minor)
[00:04:20] Priya: OK that looks promising. What about longer context, like 2k tokens?
[00:04:28] Emily: For longer context, quantization wins are still present but KV cache memory layout matters. INT8 reduces memory footprint so KV caching can be more effective; sometimes FP8 has slightly better long-range fidelity. We'll capture that in the benchmark.
[00:04:45] Marcus: For Dedicated pools — what hardware are you targeting for these numbers? A100, H100?
[00:04:52] Emily: These were A100 workhorse numbers; on H100 you can see slightly different kernel behavior. Our runtime selects kernels based on arch; we publish model-specific profiles in the console.
[00:05:10] Samir: Quick product note — Optimize will output recommended quant profiles per route and expected quality delta with a confidence interval. It's not magic; it's data driven.
[00:05:22] Liam: How do you validate — do you run adversarial prompts?
[00:05:26] Emily: We encourage customers to provide a representative prompt set and critical tests; we run regression tests and track metrics over time. For ByteWave we'd run your QA and summarization prompts.
[00:05:40] Priya: Security question — if we go Dedicated or Private, how's KMS integrated and do quantized artifacts leave the VPC?
[00:05:48] Miguel: Good one. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and optional Private deployments. Customer keys are integrated via KMS/HSM; model artifacts and logs obey your data-residency settings. Quant profiles are just config, not customer data, so they don't contain PII.
[00:06:05] Marcus: Are audit logs available for inference traces?
[00:06:08] Emily: Yes — per-route tracing, token-level latency breakdowns, and audit logs that show who invoked what. Those logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
[00:06:20] Liam: Let's talk economics — what's the cost delta between FP32, FP8, INT8 roughly?
[00:06:26] Miguel: Cost savings correlate with compute reduction. INT8 can cut per-token GPU cost substantially — up to 40-50% on certain configs due to both kernel speed and memory bandwidth. FP8 is usually 15-30% savings vs FP32. We'll send modeled pricing for your committed Dedicated pool.
[00:06:45] Priya: If we see a small quality regression, can we do partial rollout? E.g., IN production route 90% INT8, 10% FP32?
[00:06:53] Emily: Absolutely. Redwood supports canary/rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to a safer model if regression is detected. You can specify traffic splits per quant profile.
[00:07:05] Liam: Nice. Any caveats around tokenizer differences or tokenization-induced errors with quant?
[00:07:12] Emily: Not typically — quant affects internal weights, not the tokenizer. But if your workload is heavily numeric or exact-match, test carefully.
[00:07:25] [00:07:25] Miguel: Quick demo — I'll share the benchmark sheet in chat. Emily, hit the quality-vs-latency slide where we show a scatter plot of F1 vs p95.
[00:07:35] Emily: Showing slide — x-axis p95 latency, y-axis quality delta (higher is better). FP32 baseline at top-right, FP8 clustered nearer with slight quality drop, INT8 lower latency but a few outliers with bigger drops. Emphasize: outliers need per-prompt checks.
[00:07:55] Priya: Can you annotate which outliers were due to arithmetic tasks?
[00:07:58] Emily: Yes — the spreadsheet has tags. We'll mark tasks with numeric precision issues.
[00:08:10] Marcus: Operational question: does quantized model warmup change? We saw cold-start spikes previously.
[00:08:16] Emily: Cold-start/warmup behavior depends on model initialization and kernel JITs. Redwood runtime preloads warmed kernels for expected routes; for Dedicated you can reserve warm workers to avoid cold starts. Quantized kernels might JIT faster because less compute, but still recommend a warm pool for low p95.
[00:08:40] Liam: What's the recommended pilot length?
[00:08:44] Miguel: Typically a 1-week load test with your representative workload plus a short 2-week validation period for quality gating. We can compress if needed.
[00:08:55] Priya: For our internal compliance we need SOC2 + SSO and IP allowlist. Is that supported for Dedicated?
[00:09:02] Miguel: Yes. SOC2 is standard; SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported, plus IP allowlists and VPC peering for Dedicated. We'll include the security pack in the docs.
[00:09:15] Liam: Can Redwood run the pilot in our EU region? Data residency concerns.
[00:09:20] Emily: Yes — we can allocate Dedicated capacity in EU regions or run a Private deployment if required. We'll note the region in the proposal.
[00:09:30] [00:09:30] Miguel: Quick detour — anyone using embeddings heavily? Just curious because quantization effects differ for embeddings.
[00:09:35] Priya: We do for semantic search. Latency there is important but quality is critical.
[00:09:40] Emily: For embeddings we generally avoid aggressive quantization; we recommend FP8 or keeping FP32 for embedding generation to avoid vector quality loss. You can quantize downstream indexers.
[00:09:55] Marcus: How granular are quant profiles? Route-level? Model-level?
[00:09:59] Emily: Profiles are per-route and you can tie them to model variants. So for your search route you could use FP32/FP8 and for chat INT8 where acceptable.
[00:10:12] Liam: Any limits on switching profiles programmatically?
[00:10:17] Miguel: No hard limits — via API you can change routing, rollout percentages, quant profiles. Changes propagate quickly but we recommend controlled rollouts.
[00:10:28] Priya: Can we see the console now for profiles UI?
[00:10:33] Emily: Yep, sharing screen. (screen share noise) In Console -> Optimize -> Quant Profiles you get recommended profiles, per-model deltas, and an exportable CSV.
[00:10:50] [00:10:50] Emily: Here is the ByteWave example: route /generate-chat uses model x-redwood-1. By default we show baseline FP32, recommended FP8 with -0.4% quality delta, and INT8 with -1.3% delta but -40% latency.
[00:11:10] Liam: The UI shows confidence scores?
[00:11:14] Emily: Yes — we show a confidence band based on sample size and variability. Low sample size gets a low confidence.
[00:11:27] Marcus: Do you store the sample prompts we send?
[00:11:30] Miguel: Only if you opt in; samples used for eval are stored per your retention policy and can be deleted after testing. We support retention controls.
[00:11:45] Priya: If a regression is detected post-rollout, what's the rollback path?
[00:11:49] Emily: Automatic rollback is supported: either immediate fallback to previous profile or traffic split adjustment. You can set automatic quality gates e.g., no more than X delta in F1.
[00:12:05] Liam: Ok good. One more technical: how do you handle attention kernel selection for quantized runs?
[00:12:12] Emily: Runtime chooses kernels per layer; we have quant-aware kernels and some attention fusion for INT8 on Ampere architectures. It's somewhat model-specific and that's why we provide model profiles.
[00:12:30] Samir: And we keep a changelog for kernel updates — we'll surface any perf/regressions in the console.
[00:12:40] Priya: Any chance of out-of-distribution failure modes? Like catastrophic collapse for certain prompt types?
[00:12:47] Emily: It's rare but possible; that's why we recommend adversarial tests and conservative rollouts. If you have critical safety prompts, keep them on FP32 until validated.
[00:13:05] Miguel: Let's talk concrete pilot steps: Emily, we'll run your benchmarks on ByteWave's sample set on Dedicated A100 pool. We'll capture p95, throughput, and task-level QA metrics. Then we'll tune quant params and run a 1-week production-like run.
[00:13:20] Liam: Timeline wise can we start next week?
[00:13:24] Miguel: Yes — we'll send a pilot proposal today and pricing by Friday.
[00:13:30] Priya: For the sample set — do you need streaming logs or can we provide batch files?
[00:13:36] Emily: Batch files are fine for the initial run. For runtime monitoring during pilot we'll use streaming traces.
[00:13:45] Marcus: For cost estimation, include both best-case INT8 and FP8 scenarios and also fallback costs if we need FP32 for some routes.
[00:13:52] Miguel: Will do.
[00:13:56] [00:13:56] Liam: Any documentation links?
[00:13:58] Miguel: I'll drop links in the follow-up: Optimize docs, quant profile guide, security pack, and the benchmark template.
[00:14:05] Priya: Great. A couple of small clarifications: when you say INT8 do you support per-channel quantization or just symmetric?
[00:14:12] Emily: We support per-channel where it helps; our quantizer chooses between symmetric/asymmetric and per-channel/per-tensor as needed. Most of the heavy lifting is automatic but tunable.
[00:14:25] Priya: Nice. Do you expose those knobs in the console?
[00:14:28] Emily: Yes — advanced mode exposes quant knobs; otherwise we auto-select.
[00:14:36] Marcus: If we want a Private on-prem deployment how different is the process for quant workloads?
[00:14:41] Miguel: Private deploy is similar — the runtime and kernels are the same; you get full control over network and keys. We ship the same Optimize tooling.
[00:14:52] Liam: Ok that helps. Anything else from your side, Priya?
[00:14:56] Priya: No that's it. We'll provide the sample prompts by Friday.
[00:15:00] Miguel: Great. Recap and next steps — send pricing & proposal, share benchmark sheet, schedule pilot kickoff. Any blockers?
[00:15:10] Liam: None from our side.
[00:15:14] Miguel: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email.
